items.streamTitle: A U.S. appeals court upheld the Pentagon's supply-chain-risk designation of Anthropic
items.streamSummary: A U.S. appeals court upheld the Pentagon's designation of Anthropic as a national-security supply-chain risk, a decision with significant procurement and reputational consequences. The dispute centered partly on Anthropic's restrictions on certain military uses. The ruling resolves a legal stage, not the underlying technical question of whether the company's safeguards create operational risk or improve safety.

items.streamTitle: Social-media detox evidence was mixed rather than uniformly beneficial
items.streamSummary: A review of social-media detox interventions found mixed effects across wellbeing outcomes and designs. Some studies reported benefits, while others found small or null changes. The evidence does not support treating a temporary break as a universal solution to digital harms. Effects depend on the outcome, intervention, and population being measured.

items.streamTitle: Agent trace deletion reduced context burden but created state-loss risk
items.streamSummary: A preprint tested ways for long-running agents to delete or compress parts of their execution history. Selective removal can reduce context cost, but the same mechanism can discard information later needed for debugging, recovery, or verification. The work reinforces that memory optimization is a governance problem as well as a performance problem: provenance and recoverability need explicit protection.

items.streamTitle: Perceived political coalitions shaped judgments beyond simple ideology
items.streamSummary: Experiments showed that people organize political actors into perceived coalitions and use those relational structures when making judgments. The finding suggests that political cognition is not reducible to one-dimensional ideology: who is seen as allied with whom can change interpretation. The studies are controlled experiments, so the size and durability of these effects in live political environments remain separate questions.

items.streamTitle: An MCP agent-to-agent attack showed how malicious instructions can cross tool boundaries
items.streamSummary: A preprint demonstrated an agent-to-agent attack in Model Context Protocol workflows, showing how malicious content introduced in one component can influence downstream tools or agents. The result is configuration-dependent, not evidence that every MCP deployment is vulnerable. Its broader value is architectural: trust boundaries, provenance, and action authorization need to persist across the whole connected workflow.

items.streamTitle: Visual-reasoning performance varied sharply across task types
items.streamSummary: A broad analysis of visual-reasoning systems found substantial variation across task families and representations. Aggregate performance therefore hid important weaknesses that emerged only on particular reasoning demands. The practical lesson is to test the visual operations a system actually needs to perform, rather than using a single benchmark average as evidence of general visual intelligence.

items.streamTitle: Wrong AI advice reduced people's willingness to say 'I don't know'
items.streamSummary: A controlled preprint found that confident but incorrect AI advice could reduce people's use of an 'I don't know' option and pull responses toward the model. The result matters because an assistant can alter confidence behavior even when it does not improve knowledge. The evidence comes from bounded tasks rather than consequential field decisions, so transfer to professional settings needs testing.

items.streamTitle: Serious-game co-creation improved design fit but did not by itself prove behavioral impact
items.streamSummary: A Scientific Reports study described a stakeholder co-creation process for a serious game, showing how iterative participation can surface usability and implementation needs that designers might otherwise miss. The work supports co-creation as a development method, not as evidence that a co-created game automatically changes behavior. Outcome testing remains a separate stage.

items.streamTitle: Micro-randomized intervention data supported adaptive machine-learning decisions without abandoning experimentation
items.streamSummary: A study combined micro-randomized intervention opportunities with machine-learning decision rules, preserving randomized variation while exploring more personalized treatment timing. The approach is useful because it separates prediction from causal learning better than purely observational personalization. Results remain specific to the tested setting, and deployment still requires calibration and monitoring.

items.streamTitle: UK firms gained access to Ukraine's Avengers Labs data for AI drone-swarm development
items.streamSummary: The UK launched a competition allowing selected companies to use Ukraine's Avengers Labs battlefield datasets to develop AI-enabled drone swarms and collaborative autonomy. The initiative creates a concrete data-sharing and testing pathway between wartime experience and allied industry. It does not yet show that the resulting models improve swarm performance or survive contested conditions; those outcomes require later testing.

items.streamTitle: Ukraine began testing SPECTR to turn combat data into planning recommendations
items.streamSummary: Ukraine's Defense AI Center A1 is developing SPECTR to analyze battlefield data, identify patterns, generate planning recommendations, and reduce headquarters routine work. Several combat units were already testing the system. Officials also described a goal of predicting enemy actions, but no public forecast accuracy, calibration, or mission-effect results were released. The development shows integration of AI into staff workflows rather than demonstrated battlefield superiority.

items.streamTitle: The Navy created a dedicated warfighting center to integrate robotic and autonomous systems
items.streamSummary: The U.S. Navy established a Robotics and Autonomous Systems Warfighting Development Center to turn distributed unmanned-system experimentation into shared concepts, training, testing, and tactics. The center is intended to bridge development and operational employment and to test systems under realistic conditions. This is an institutional readiness milestone, not evidence that any specific autonomous platform is effective in combat.

items.streamTitle: EgoSpeedUp accelerated embodied-agent simulation while trying to preserve task fidelity
items.streamSummary: EgoSpeedUp proposes techniques for faster egocentric embodied-agent simulation. The reported results show meaningful runtime reductions in the tested environments while preserving key task outputs. For simulation-heavy research, the important question is not speed alone but whether acceleration changes the dynamics being studied. Fidelity, determinism, and downstream policy performance should therefore accompany runtime claims.

items.streamTitle: An R0-style social metric quantified clustered blood-pressure risk without proving contagion
items.streamSummary: A study adapted an R0-style framework to social-network patterns in blood pressure. The metric summarized how risk clustered through social exposure, but the design does not show that hypertension literally spreads from person to person. The methodological value is in representing propagation-like social structure while keeping causal transmission separate from statistical clustering.

items.streamTitle: NNV3 targeted more efficient structured visual reasoning
items.streamSummary: NNV3 is a preprint proposing a more efficient neural architecture for structured visual reasoning. Reported benchmark results suggest useful gains, but the evidence remains limited to the tested tasks and does not establish reliability in operational imagery or unfamiliar environments. The practical lesson is to evaluate efficiency and generalization together rather than treating reduced compute as a standalone capability gain.

items.streamTitle: Adaptive graph modeling improved cross-domain hate-speech detection in benchmark tests
items.streamSummary: AdaGraph-HATE adapts graph representations to classify hate speech across changing domains. The reported experiments improved transfer relative to comparison methods, but the gains remain benchmark-specific and depend on how the graph and target domain are represented. The work is relevant to information-environment analysis because language and network context can shift together; live adversarial robustness still requires separate validation.

items.streamTitle: Backward reasoning over AND-OR structures improved structured search in benchmark problems
items.streamSummary: A methods paper developed backward reasoning over AND-OR structures to solve complex problems by tracing goals through explicit alternatives and dependencies. Reported results improved search on the tested problems, but the model inherits the quality of its representation. For decision support, the value is transparent decomposition rather than automatic proof that the encoded graph is complete or causally correct.

items.streamTitle: Land acknowledgements produced narrower effects than their symbolic prominence might imply
items.streamSummary: A randomized study tested whether land acknowledgements change downstream attitudes and responses. Effects were limited and outcome-specific rather than uniformly positive. The result is useful for separating institutional signaling from measurable behavioral impact: a message can be highly visible without producing broad change, and null outcomes should remain visible when evaluating symbolic interventions.

items.streamTitle: Fair process and shared benefits mattered more than carbon-removal capacity for public support
items.streamSummary: Consulting local people or experts increased support by about 1.0–1.7 points on a ten-point scale relative to no consultation. Community benefit sharing and public-service arrangements also raised support. Higher removal capacity helped, but generally did not compensate for unfair procedures or distribution. These are stated responses to hypothetical projects, not observed acceptance of built facilities. Legitimacy is part of implementation, not a communications add-on. A model of technology adoption should represent decision process, trust, and who receives benefits separately from technical performance; field settings may produce stronger conflict than these unfamiliar vignettes.
items.attribution: Fritz et al. — Nature Climate Change

items.streamTitle: A simulated X ranking rule amplified low-credibility links through easy reactions
items.streamSummary: In their model, predicted likes and reposts could substitute for replies and quotes in a weighted engagement score, favoring content that elicited quick reactions. Weight tuning had little or adverse effect in simulations; a threshold requiring predicted reflective engagement reduced the low-credibility exposure gap without reducing modeled mainstream exposure or engagement. This is an unreviewed preprint and a calibrated reimplementation, not a live platform intervention. A ranking system can shape exposure through the way it combines behavior signals, even if no single signal is explicitly labeled as misinformation. Platform-level causal claims require live validation and careful treatment of source-credibility labels.

items.streamTitle: A Canadian climate-news corpus provides frame labels with category-level reliability
items.streamSummary: On a 1,000-sentence independently double-coded reference set, the pooled macro F1 was 0.866, while mean per-category macro F1 was 0.773; categories were assigned A/B/C reliability tiers. These metrics describe annotation performance, not proof of media effects on public opinion. Coverage is Canadian and source selection matters. The corpus is a useful design pattern for PSYWERX discourse maps: publish a taxonomy, human coding reference, category-specific uncertainty, and reusable data together. Trend analyses should account for changing outlet coverage and weaker classes.

items.streamTitle: Selective human review can make AI-assisted hypothesis tests cheaper while controlling error
items.streamSummary: The authors prove finite-sample validity under their model and show near-optimal asymptotic cost as target errors tighten. Numerical studies found the largest savings when cheap AI reports and selective human checks both contributed. These are formal and simulated results, not evidence of savings or accuracy in a deployed PSYWERX review queue. Human review is most useful where the AI report changes the value of verification. A pilot with paired human and AI labels would be needed to estimate the error model and test whether the theoretical saving transfers to an actual research workflow.

items.streamTitle: LLM conversation judges needed anchors to make their scores comparable
items.streamSummary: Pointwise scores correlated moderately with human ratings, while pairwise comparisons suffered from long transcripts and position bias. The new dataset showed a gap between current judges and human discrimination. Calibration placed judges on a shared scale and transferred to the human-AI dataset in their tests; it did not make the judges equivalent to human evaluators. Evaluation scores should carry a calibration protocol and a human reference. In PSYWERX-style human-AI assessments, compare stable anchor cases and inspect order effects before treating score differences as substantive.

items.streamTitle: NATO framed interoperability as preparation that must precede multi-domain operations
items.streamSummary: The publication lays out an operational approach and implementation logic: interoperability and resilience must be built and exercised before crisis, while nations retain authority over what they share. It reports no controlled comparison or measured advantage from a new deployment. Its discussion of the cognitive dimension is conceptual rather than an observed influence effect. For information advantage, speed is an end-to-end property of sensing, sharing, deciding, and acting, subject to governance and trust. Evaluation should test degraded communications, data-sharing permissions, and cross-national handoffs rather than count connected tools alone.
